page.layout: One column of running text. Above it: running head at top left, page number at top right. Centred below them: the sermon heading "CONCIO VI", then the scripture reference "Genef. 20." set apart. Body is one text block with a decorated initial. No marginal notes. Signature "E" at the foot.

l.i: Tprofectus est inde (ex Ma-
bre) Abraham in terram
australem, habitauitq; inter
Cades, & inter Sur, & pere-
grinatus est in Gerar. Dixitq; Abra-
ham de Sara uxore sua: Soror mea
est: & misit Abimelech rex Gerar, & tulit
Saram. Venit autem Deus ad Abimelech
in somnio noctis, & dixit ad eum: Ecce tu
morieris propter mulierem quam accepi-
sti, est enim marito iuncta. Abimelech
vero non accesserat ad eam: & ait: Do-
mine, num quid interficies quoque gen-
tem iustam? An non ipse dixit mihi,
soror mea est? cum integritate cordis mei,
& cum innocentia manuum mearum fe-
ci hoc. Dixitq; ad eum Deus per somni-
um: Etiam ego novi, quòd in integritate
cordis tui feceris hoc, & prohibui etiam
ego te, ne peccares in me, atque ideo non
permisi ut tangeres eam. Nunc igitur
restitue uxorem viro, est enim propheta,
& orabit pro te, ut vivas: quòd si non re-
stitueris, scito quòd moriendo morieris et

page.notes: Small reference signs (a stroke-and-circle mark, printed before "Abraham" and "Abimelech") are not transcribed; they are printing marks, not words. The large initial "T" is decorative and joined to "profectus" as the rule for woodcut initials requires. Long s and s read as plain s throughout. The line "Saram. Venit" and "Dixitq;" are as printed. Continues on the next page mid-sentence ("et").
